name: cache-aside-miss-and-outage
description: Tests that a cache read treats redis.Nil as a miss, falls back to the database on other errors, and sets a TTL
prompt: Add a Redis cache in front of GetItem(ctx, id) in our Go service using go-redis v9. Items are read far more often than they change.
trap: Without the skill, the model often returns err on redis.Nil (every miss fails), compares err == redis.Nil, writes the value with Set(..., 0), or fails the request when Redis is down.

assertions.text: Matches the miss with errors.Is(err, redis.Nil), not ==, and treats it as a miss
On any other Redis error, logs it and serves from the database instead of failing the request
Writes the cached value with a non-zero TTL (ideally jittered)
Protects against a stampede on a hot key (singleflight or equivalent)
Invalidates by deleting the key after the database write commits, not before and not by writing the new value

name: client-construction
description: Tests one client per process built from settings with context deadlines honoured
prompt: Our handlers each do redis.NewClient(&redis.Options{Addr: os.Getenv("REDIS_ADDR")}) and call rdb.Get(context.Background(), key). Clean this up.
trap: Without the skill, the model may keep a client per request, move it to a package-level global, keep context.Background(), or miss that go-redis ignores ctx deadlines on the socket unless ContextTimeoutEnabled is set.

assertions.text: Builds one client at startup and passes it to the handlers through a constructor, not a package-level variable
Closes the client on shutdown, after the HTTP server has stopped
Passes the request's context (r.Context()) to every command
Sets ContextTimeoutEnabled: true and keeps dial, read and write timeouts set
Reads the address and credentials from the service's settings (a password file or secret), not hard-coded

name: distributed-lock
description: Tests a Redis lock with a token, a TTL and a token-checked release, and the caveat about correctness
prompt: We run three replicas and a nightly invoice job must only run on one of them. Implement it with Redis.
trap: Without the skill, the model may use SETNX with no expiry, release with a plain DEL, or present the lock as a correctness guarantee.

assertions.text: Acquires with SET NX and an expiry (SetNX with a TTL > 0) and a random token per holder
Releases with a Lua script (or DELEX IFEQ) that deletes only if the key still holds the token
Says the lock prevents duplicate work but isn't a correctness guarantee, and makes the job safe to run twice or adds a database check
Does not adopt Redlock

name: stream-consumer
description: Tests a Redis Streams consumer group that acknowledges after processing and reclaims pending entries
prompt: Consume order events from the Redis stream orders:events in a Go worker so each event is handled once even if a worker crashes.
trap: Without the skill, the model may use Pub/Sub, set NoAck, acknowledge before handling, or never reclaim pending entries of a dead consumer.

assertions.text: Uses a consumer group with XReadGroup and the ">" ID, creating the group with MKSTREAM and ignoring BUSYGROUP
Calls XAck only after the handler succeeds; no NoAck: true
Reclaims entries left pending by a dead consumer with XAutoClaim (or XClaim)
States delivery is at least once and makes the handler idempotent
Explains that Pub/Sub would lose events while a subscriber is down

name: delete-by-pattern
description: Tests SCAN and UNLINK instead of KEYS
prompt: Write a Go function that deletes all session keys for a customer: they match orders:session:<customer-id>:*.
trap: Without the skill, the model often calls rdb.Keys(ctx, pattern) and Del, which blocks the server on a large keyspace and fails across slots on a cluster.

assertions.text: Uses SCAN with MATCH and a COUNT (the go-redis ScanIterator), not KEYS
Deletes in batches with UNLINK (or DEL in small batches)
Checks the iterator's Err() after the loop
Mentions that on a cluster the scan runs per primary (ForEachMaster), or that a hash tag or a per-customer set avoids scanning
